before.title: 718 Cayman (982) Early Turbo-Four High Oil Consumption
before.description: A number of early 2.0L and 2.5L turbocharged flat-four 718 engines consume oil at a high rate — owners report roughly a quart per 1,000 miles, with the worst cases needing engine replacement under warranty. Some 2019 2.0L cars also suffered oil-separator (PCV) diaphragm failures that let oil be drawn into the cylinders, sometimes appearing right after an oil and filter change.
before.solution: Document consumption with a Porsche oil-consumption test. Replace a failed air-oil separator / PCV diaphragm. Severely affected engines were replaced under warranty by Porsche; otherwise monitor level closely and top up with the correct specification oil between services.
symptoms: Needing to top up oil between services

before.title: 718 Cayman (982) Gasoline Particulate Filter (GPF/OPF) Failure
before.description: EU-spec 718 Caymans built from the 2019 model year onward carry a gasoline particulate filter integrated into the catalytic converter assembly. A production-era software fault plus high oil-ash loading causes the GPF to clog and fail, often with no warning light beforehand. Because the GPF is bonded to the cat, replacement is extremely expensive, and Porsche classifies particulate filters as service/wear items excluded from warranty — a major pain point for European owners.
before.solution: Confirm the fault via diagnostics. Apply the updated GPF/OPF software where available and fit the revised filter (e.g. part 982 254 400 AF designed to resist the problem). Use the correct low-ash specification oil and avoid only short trips. Failed units require GPF/cat assembly replacement.
symptoms: Sudden failure with no prior warning

before.title: AC Compressor Failure and Clutch Burnout
before.description: The AC compressor on the Cayman fails prematurely, often due to clutch bearing wear or internal seal failure. The mid-engine layout subjects the AC system to higher ambient temperatures. When the compressor clutch fails, it can throw the serpentine belt and disable all accessories.
before.solution: Replace the AC compressor and receiver/drier. Flush the AC system of any debris from the failed compressor. Replace the expansion valve as preventive maintenance. Ensure proper refrigerant charge after repair.
symptoms: Clicking or grinding noise when AC engages
Burning rubber smell from accessory belt area

citations.title: Planet-9.com — Cayman AC compressor failure patterns and replacement guide

communityRecommendations.content: Run the AC system for at least 10 minutes every month, even in winter, to keep the compressor seals lubricated and prevent premature failure.

before.title: Cylinder Bore Scoring
before.description: The Cayman M97 and MA1 flat-six engines develop bore scoring on cylinders 1 and 6, identical to the pattern seen in the 911 and Boxster. The Cayman GT4 with its 3.8L 911-derived engine is also affected. Oil starvation at the cylinder walls during cold starts is the primary cause.
before.solution: Engine rebuild with iron cylinder sleeves (Nickies) or engine replacement. Regular borescope inspections can detect scoring before it becomes catastrophic. Allow full warm-up before spirited driving.

before.title: Coolant Expansion Tank and Cap Failure / Cooling System Leaks
before.description: The plastic coolant expansion (header) tank develops hairline cracks at the seams from heat cycling and age, and the pressure cap frequently fails — losing seal and letting the system lose pressure. The result is slow coolant loss that often evaporates off hot components without leaving a visible puddle, plus air pockets and localized boiling. The 2.7L/3.4L engines also have a plastic coolant cross-over pipe whose rubber block seals degrade and weep down the front of the engine.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system. Replace the cracked expansion tank and the pressure cap together (the cap fails about half the time and is cheap to do alongside). Reseal or replace the plastic coolant pipe seals if leaking. Bleed the system afterward.
symptoms: Slow coolant loss with no visible leak
White scale deposits near pipe/pump seals

before.title: Front Radiator / A/C Condenser Corrosion and Debris-Trapped Leaks
before.description: The twin radiators and A/C condensers sit low behind the front bumper grilles, directly in the path of road debris, leaves, and salt. Debris packs between the condenser and radiator, traps moisture, and corrodes the aluminum until it perforates; rocks also puncture the exposed fins. The result is gradual coolant or refrigerant loss and, eventually, overheating or a dead A/C system. German owner sources specifically note the front radiators 'corrode and spring leaks' on the 987.
before.solution: Clean trapped debris from the bumper ducts (typical shop charge around USD 300), and replace the corroded radiator and/or A/C condenser, then re-gas the A/C. Many owners fit aftermarket radiator/condenser protective grilles or screens behind the bumper intakes to prevent recurrence.
symptoms: Gradual coolant loss with no obvious puddle
Debris and corrosion visible in bumper intakes

before.title: Front Suspension Clunk — Control Arms, Sway Bar Bushings, Drop Links
before.description: Higher-mileage cars develop a clunk or rattle over bumps at low speed. Common culprits are worn lower-control-arm ball joints and bushings, a sway (anti-roll) bar that has gone loose inside its rubber mount bushings, and worn drop links (sway bar end links). Owners frequently chase the noise to the sway bar bushing after replacing other parts. Rear clunks trace to a loose sway bar or a trailing-arm bushing.
before.solution: Inspect for play with the car lifted. Replace worn drop links first (cheap DIY), and renew sway bar mount bushings, lower control arms / ball joints, and tie rod ends as needed. A four-wheel alignment is required after control arm replacement.
symptoms: Clunk or knock over bumps at low speed

before.title: Ignition Switch Failure / No-Start (Key Not Responding)
before.description: The electrical ignition switch behind the lock cylinder wears out, so turning the key produces nothing — no dash lights, no steering-lock click, no crank. The lock cylinder can also become stiff, fail to return, or trap the key. It is a well-documented 987 Cayman/Boxster fault discussed across English and German (PFF.de) owner forums.
before.solution: Replace the electrical portion of the ignition switch (a relatively inexpensive, straightforward part behind the lock barrel) — this usually cures the no-start immediately. In persistent cases the lock cylinder is replaced as well.
symptoms: No crank, no dash lights when key is turned
Key stiff or stuck in ignition

before.title: PDK Dual-Clutch Mechatronic / Clutch-Pack Faults
before.description: The 7-speed PDK can develop jerky or delayed shifting, shudder, or drop into limp/emergency mode. The most common root causes are mechatronic-unit problems (the hydraulic valve body, solenoids, and the distance/position sensors that are the most frequent failure point) and, with miles, clutch-pack wear. On the 981 specifically, owners report it limping home with reduced gears.
before.solution: Diagnose with a Porsche scan tool. Service the PDK fluid and filter on schedule. Repair or rebuild the mechatronic unit (valve body / sensors / solenoids) — now repairable for a fraction of full transmission replacement — and replace worn clutch packs as needed.
symptoms: Loss of reverse or specific gears

before.title: Rear Main Seal (RMS) Oil Leak
before.description: The crankshaft rear main seal between the engine and transmission weeps oil, which appears as drips from the bell-housing seam. On the M96/M97 flat-six it is frequently aggravated by a failing air-oil separator that pushes crankcase pressure too high under hard acceleration, damaging the seal. Left unaddressed, oil migrates onto the clutch friction surface and contaminates it.
before.solution: Replace the rear main seal (engine/transmission must be separated). Because the gearbox is already removed, owners and shops strongly recommend replacing the clutch at the same time, and many also replace the IMS bearing and check the AOS while the drivetrain is apart to consolidate labor.
symptoms: Oil spots on garage floor near transmission
